json.title: [P1] First-class multi-database orchestration in self-host mode
json.body:
## Problem

The cloud orchestrator manages a pipeline per project (`pipeline_manager.rs`), but self-host entry points are single-database: `ensureEngine({ databaseUrl })` in `@syncrabbit/node`, one `DATABASE_URL` in the Next.js integration. A database-per-tenant customer (real evaluation case: ~100 tenant databases on one RDS instance) has no supported way to run N pipelines from one self-hosted engine.

## Fix

- Node SDK: `ensureEngine({ databases: [{ id, databaseUrl }] })` + register/deregister at runtime (tenant onboarding).
- One WS endpoint with per-database scoping (pairs with connection auth: token claims bind a connection to a database id).
- Document slot + connection budgets at N databases on one Postgres instance (each pipeline = 1 replication slot + 1 replication connection).

## Acceptance

- 100 registered databases on one instance: bounded connections, per-database slot metrics, runtime add/remove without engine restart.

## Design proposal: expose the orchestration that already exists

From a database-per-tenant evaluation (NestJS + Next.js monorepo, ~100 tenant databases on one RDS instance). Pairs with the auth design in #14.

### Most of this is already built

`PipelineManager` (`infra/crates/orchestrator/src/pipeline_manager.rs`) already does what this issue asks for. It holds a `DashMap<String, ProjectConfig>` where each config carries its own `database_url`, `slot_name`, and `publication_name`; it starts pipelines on demand; and `register_project` / `unregister_project` (`pipeline_manager.rs:67,72`) are exactly the runtime add/remove that tenant onboarding needs. They're already exposed over an admin-authenticated HTTP API at `POST /admin/pipelines/{id}/start` and `/stop` (`infra/crates/orchestrator/src/admin.rs:104,125`).

The gap is purely reachability. The self-host binary is a different crate — `syncrabbit-server` — and its `Serve` command takes a single `--database-url` (`infra/crates/server/src/config.rs:16-27`), builds one `PostgresAdapter`, and never touches `PipelineManager`. `ensureEngine` (`packages/node-sdk/src/singleton.ts:24`) and the Next.js SDK (`packages/nextjs-sdk/src/server.ts:35`) inherit that single-database shape.

So the work is: **lift `PipelineManager` out of the orchestrator crate into `syncrabbit-engine` (or its own `syncrabbit-pipeline` crate), and have `syncrabbit-server` drive it instead of a bare adapter.** Both entry points then share one multi-database implementation, and the cloud/self-host divergence in this area disappears rather than being duplicated.

### Node SDK surface

```ts
export interface DatabaseConfig {
  id: string;                  // stable, non-secret id. carried as the `sr_db` token claim (#14)
  databaseUrl: string;
  slotName?: string;           // default: "syncrabbit_slot"
  publicationName?: string;    // default: "syncrabbit_pub"
}

export interface EngineOptions {
  databases?: DatabaseConfig[];
  databaseUrl?: string;        // sugar for [{ id: "default", databaseUrl }]. keeps every existing caller working.
  // ...existing fields
}
```

plus runtime registration on the returned manager, for tenant onboarding without an engine restart:

```ts
const engine = getOrCreateEngine({ databases: [...] });
await engine.registerDatabase({ id: "tenant_42", databaseUrl });
await engine.unregisterDatabase("tenant_42");
```

These call the local admin API with the admin secret the SDK already generates when it spawns the engine process — no new control plane, just a client for the one in `admin.rs`.

On slot naming: Postgres logical replication slots are **per-database**, so `syncrabbit_slot` in each tenant database does not collide, and the existing default is safe. What is *not* per-database is `max_replication_slots` and `max_wal_senders` — those are instance-wide. At 100 tenant databases on one instance you need both ≥ 100, and the RDS defaults (often 10) will stop you long before then. That's a parameter-group change plus a reboot, so it belongs in preflight (`infra/crates/adapters/postgres/src/preflight.rs`) as a hard check against the number of registered databases, not just a doc note.

### The tension with #18 that needs resolving before either lands

#18 correctly wants to replace stop-on-idle with **consume-and-discard**, so an idle project's slot keeps advancing `confirmed_flush_lsn` and stops pinning WAL. But "keep consuming" means "keep a walsender connection open," and at 100 registered tenant databases that is 100 permanent replication connections — which is precisely the budget this issue says must stay bounded. Taken naively, #18's fix breaks #21's acceptance criterion.

Suggested resolution: **periodic drain instead of continuous drain.** An idle pipeline (zero subscribers) is not held open; instead a scheduler wakes it every `T` seconds, connects, consumes and discards to advance `confirmed_flush_lsn`, and disconnects. WAL retention is then bounded by `T × write_rate` rather than by "forever," and the steady-state connection cost for idle tenants is zero. Active tenants keep a live pipeline as today. `T` on the order of minutes bounds WAL to something small on any realistic write rate, and the drain sweep can be concurrency-limited (say 8 at a time) so a hundred idle tenants don't stampede the instance.

That also replaces, rather than tunes, the current `STOP_GRACE_PERIOD` (`pipeline_manager.rs:15`) — the grace period exists to avoid pipeline thrash on brief disconnects, and a drain scheduler makes idleness cheap enough that the grace period stops carrying that weight alone.

### Interaction with auth (#14)

The token claim `sr_db` **is** the database selector: a connection authenticated for `tenant_42` gets `get_or_create_ws_state("tenant_42")` and therefore that tenant's `SubscriptionManager` and `Sieve`. Cross-tenant fanout becomes structurally impossible rather than filter-enforced. That's why these two issues want to land together — shipping multi-database registration while the id still arrives from an untrusted subdomain (`infra/crates/orchestrator/src/ws.rs:60-75`) would let a client pick which tenant's database it listens to.

`sr_db` is optional and defaults to `"default"`, so single-database adopters — the majority — never encounter the concept at all. Multi-database registration is opt-in surface area, not a tax on the simple case.
